test_baseline.windows_git_bash: 1 failure at tests/smoke.sh:245 (chmod 500 cannot make a directory unwritable on Windows); all other cases pass

acceptance.criterion: `herdr-plugin.toml` declares platforms linux, macos, and windows.
acceptance.evidence: herdr-plugin.toml:6 reads platforms = ["linux", "macos", "windows"].

acceptance.criterion: The action id stays `open`, the pane id stays `helper`, the pane title stays `Lantern`, and the placement stays `tab`.
acceptance.evidence: herdr plugin link returned actions[0].id=open, panes[0].id=helper, panes[0].title=Lantern, panes[0].placement=tab. tests/smoke.sh:49,70,71 assert placement and title and passed in the same run.

acceptance.criterion: `herdr plugin action list` reports windows in the action platforms after relink.
acceptance.evidence: After uninstalling the GitHub copy and linking C:\Claude\herdr-lantern, herdr plugin action list returned "platforms":["linux","macos","windows"].

acceptance.criterion: `bin/herdr.cmd` forwards its arguments to the POSIX wrapper through `sh.exe` and exits with the wrapper's exit code.
acceptance.evidence: tests/smoke.sh runs `herdr.cmd agent list` against a stub that exits 7 and asserts status 7. Passes.

acceptance.criterion: A mutating command through `bin/herdr.cmd` without `HERDR_HELPER_OK` exits non-zero and prints the `HERDR_HELPER_OK` hint.
acceptance.evidence: tests/smoke.sh asserts `workspace create` through herdr.cmd fails and that stderr carries the HERDR_HELPER_OK hint. Confirmed by hand at exit 2 before the test existed.

acceptance.criterion: An inspect command through `bin/herdr.cmd` reaches the real herdr.
acceptance.evidence: tests/smoke.sh asserts the stub printed `real herdr agent list`. By hand against the live binary, `cmd /c bin\herdr.cmd agent list` returned the agent_list JSON.

acceptance.criterion: With both files present, Git Bash `command -v herdr` still selects the extensionless wrapper.
acceptance.evidence: tests/smoke.sh asserts `PATH=$root/bin:$PATH command -v herdr` equals `$root/bin/herdr`. Passes with bin/herdr.cmd present.

acceptance.criterion: `bin/herdr.cmd` never falls through to the real herdr when `sh.exe` is missing.
acceptance.evidence: tests/smoke.sh runs herdr.cmd from a batch file with PATH, ProgramFiles, ProgramFiles(x86) and LOCALAPPDATA scrubbed: exit 127, stderr says `refusing to run herdr`, and neither stream contains `real herdr`.

acceptance.criterion: `lib.sh` has `helper_detect_python`, which rejects a zero-byte candidate and validates each candidate by running it.
acceptance.evidence: lib.sh helper_detect_python skips a candidate failing `[ -s ]` and requires `sys.version_info[0] == 3` from a real run. tests/smoke.sh puts a zero-byte python3 first on PATH and asserts detection does not return python3.

acceptance.criterion: `launch.sh` uses the detected interpreter for `bin/goals-floor` and `bin/elves-floor`.
acceptance.evidence: launch.sh calls helper_detect_python once and uses $helper_python for both scripts. tests/smoke.sh asserts launch.sh mentions helper_detect_python and no longer calls python3 against $plugin_root.

acceptance.criterion: A missing interpreter skips the snapshot and never kills the pane.
acceptance.evidence: Detection failure falls to `helper_python=` and the block is guarded by `[ -n "$helper_python" ]`. launch.sh runs under `set -u` only, so no failure path exits.

acceptance.criterion: `bin/goals-floor` decodes herdr output as UTF-8 with replacement, so pane text carrying box drawing or emoji cannot crash the snapshot on a Windows code page.
acceptance.evidence: run_herdr now passes encoding="utf-8", errors="replace". tests/smoke.sh feeds goals-floor a fixture containing ※ and ◎ through a native stub and asserts herd_detected 1, NEEDS YOU, and /goal 2h.

acceptance.criterion: `lib.sh` has `helper_native_path`, which converts with `cygpath -w` when cygpath exists and is identity otherwise.
`open.sh` passes the native form to `herdr workspace create --cwd`.
`helper_normalize_root` keeps POSIX form, because `launch.sh:95` tests it with `[ -d ]`.
`helper_resolve_real_herdr` accepts a Windows-style `HERDR_BIN_PATH` and returns a path that runs.
It never returns the plugin's own wrapper.
`helper_extend_user_path` leaves macOS and Linux behaviour unchanged and adds no entry that could resolve bare `bash` to the WSL stub.

batches.note: B7-A2 needs a Linux and macOS run. .github/workflows/tests.yml adds an ubuntu, macos, windows matrix so the PR proves it instead of arguing it. Close this batch when that run is green.

acceptance.evidence: After `chmod 500`, the test probes with `mkdir "$open_state/probe"`. On this machine it succeeds, so the suite prints `SKIP: platform ignores directory permission bits (unlockable state dir)` and continues.

acceptance.criterion: That case still runs and passes on Linux and macOS.
acceptance.evidence: NOT VERIFIED BY EXECUTION. No Linux or macOS host was available in this session. By construction the probe mkdir fails inside a 0500 directory on those platforms, so the elif branch runs run_open and the original assertion is unchanged. This is reasoning, not a run, and it is called out in the PR.

acceptance.criterion: The suite uses the detected Python instead of a bare `python3`.
acceptance.evidence: tests/smoke.sh resolves $smoke_python from helper_detect_python and uses it for elves-floor, py_compile, and goals-floor. No bare python3 call remains in the suite.

acceptance.criterion: The full suite passes under Git Bash on Windows with the plain Windows PATH.
acceptance.evidence: `& 'C:\Program Files\Git\bin\sh.exe' tests/smoke.sh` from PowerShell prints the SKIP line, `ok: windows herdr.cmd gate`, and `ok`, then exits 0.

acceptance.criterion: `README.md` documents the Windows requirements: Herdr on Windows, Git for Windows, `C:\Program Files\Git\bin` on PATH, one helper CLI on PATH.
`README.md` gives a Windows equivalent for the `hsh` symlink step.
`CHANGELOG.md` has a 0.4.0 entry covering Windows support and the gate fix.
`herdr-plugin.toml` and the README version line both read 0.4.0.
The linked plugin creates a workspace labelled `🔥 lantern` with cwd `C:\Users\Megan` and a tab named `home`.
`claude.exe` starts in the plugin state workdir and the prompt files are written.
A second open focuses the existing chat instead of seating a second one.
The mutation gate blocks a mutating herdr command from Git Bash and from cmd.
`.gitattributes` pins the shell files, `hsh`, and `bin/herdr` to `eol=lf`, and `bin/herdr.cmd` to `eol=crlf`.
acceptance.evidence: `.gitattributes` sets `* text=auto eol=lf`, names `*.sh`, `hsh`, `bin/herdr`, `bin/goals-floor`, `bin/elves-floor` as `eol=lf`, and `*.cmd`/`*.bat` as `eol=crlf`. `git check-attr -a launch.sh` returns `text: set` and `eol: lf`.

acceptance.criterion: After renormalizing, the working tree copies of `launch.sh`, `open.sh`, `lib.sh`, `bin/herdr`, `hsh`, and `tests/smoke.sh` hold no CR bytes on this Windows checkout.
acceptance.evidence: Byte scan of all eight interpreted files reports CR=0 each, down from CR=208/167/286/33/9/387/262/262. `git ls-files --eol launch.sh lib.sh` reports `i/lf w/lf attr/text eol=lf`.

acceptance.criterion: `tests/smoke.sh` passes under Git Bash after the renormalization.
acceptance.evidence: `& 'C:\Program Files\Git\bin\sh.exe' tests/smoke.sh` still fails only at the pre-existing tests/smoke.sh:245 case that Batch 7 repairs. No new failure was introduced.

acceptance.criterion: The renormalization changes line endings only, with no content change in those files.
acceptance.evidence: `git add --renormalize .` staged nothing but `.gitattributes`, because the committed blobs were already LF. After the working-tree rewrite, `git diff --stat` is empty and `git status --short` is clean.

master_acceptance.criterion: Lantern opens and runs on Windows through Git Bash, with no change to macOS or Linux behaviour.
The herdr mutation gate cannot be bypassed on Windows by a native process resolving `herdr` on PATH.
`tests/smoke.sh` passes on Windows under Git Bash and stays valid for Linux and macOS.
`README.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` describe the Windows requirements and the release.
The repository pins the line endings its shell code depends on, so a Windows checkout cannot silently produce CRLF scripts.
